name: The Philippian jailer
charge: Believing on the Lord with all his house the same night; washing the stripes of the men he had put in the stocks
summary: He thrust Paul and Silas into the inner prison and made their feet fast in the stocks. At midnight they sang, the earthquake opened every door, and he drew his sword to kill himself. Paul cried out that they were all there. He fell down trembling, asked what he must do to be saved, was told, and before dawn had washed their wounds, been baptized with all his house, set meat before them, and rejoiced.
offense: Sirs, what must I do to be saved? And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house. And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, straightway. And when he had brought them into his house, he set meat before them.
judgment: And rejoiced, believing in God with all his house. The prisoners he had chained became his guests, the sword he had drawn on himself went back in its sheath, and the magistrates who had beaten Roman citizens uncondemned came the next morning to beg them to leave. The church at Philippi that Lydia opened her house to had a jailer in it.

entries.commentary: Blow the trumpet in Zion and sound an alarm, for the day of the Lord comes, a day of darkness and gloominess, of clouds and thick darkness. A great and strong people, the likes of which has never been, comes as a devouring army. They run like mighty men and climb the wall like men of war, keeping their ranks; the earth quakes, the heavens tremble, and the sun, moon, and stars are darkened before the Lord's very great camp, for the day of the Lord is great and terrible, and who can abide it.

Even now the Most High says to turn to him with all the heart, with fasting, weeping, and mourning, and to rend the heart and not the garments, for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and may return and leave a blessing behind him. Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, gather the people, the elders, the children, and the nursing infants, and let the priests weep between the porch and the altar and say, Spare thy people, O Lord.

Then the Lord is jealous for his land and pities his people, promising to send corn, wine, and oil until they are satisfied, and to remove the northern army far off into a barren and desolate land. He restores the years that the locust, cankerworm, caterpillar, and palmerworm have eaten, his great army which he sent among them, so his people shall eat in plenty, praise his name, and never be ashamed, and shall know that he is in the midst of Israel and that he is the Lord their God and none else.

Afterward the Most High will pour out his spirit upon all flesh, so that sons and daughters prophesy, old men dream dreams, and young men see visions, poured out even upon the servants and handmaids. He will show wonders in the heavens and earth, blood, fire, and pillars of smoke, and the sun turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the great and terrible day of the Lord; whosoever calls on the name of the Lord shall be delivered, for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance among the remnant whom the Lord shall call.

verses.text: And the multitude rose up together against them: and the magistrates rent off their clothes, and commanded to beat them.
And when they had laid many stripes upon them, they cast them into prison, charging the jailor to keep them safely:
Who, having received such a charge, thrust them into the inner prison, and made their feet fast in the stocks.
And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.
And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one’s bands were loosed.
And the keeper of the prison awaking out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, he drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled.
But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm: for we are all here.
Then he called for a light, and sprang in, and came trembling, and fell down before Paul and Silas,
And brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved?
And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.
And they spake unto him the word of the Lord, and to all that were in his house.
And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, straightway.
And when he had brought them into his house, he set meat before them, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.
And when it was day, the magistrates sent the serjeants, saying, Let those men go.
And the keeper of the prison told this saying to Paul, The magistrates have sent to let you go: now therefore depart, and go in peace.

But Paul said unto them, They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast us into prison; and now do they thrust us out privily? nay verily; but let them come themselves and fetch us out.
And the serjeants told these words unto the magistrates: and they feared, when they heard that they were Romans.
And they came and besought them, and brought them out, and desired them to depart out of the city.
And they went out of the prison, and entered into the house of Lydia: and when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them, and departed.
The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.

And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be delivered: for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as the Lord hath said, and in the remnant whom the Lord shall call.
